title: Machine Learning Foundations Test
description: Test your machine learning knowledge: supervised vs unsupervised, gradient descent, loss functions, metrics, and tuning.

questions.question: What is Gradient Descent in machine learning?
options: An iterative optimization algorithm for finding the minimum of a differentiable loss function by taking steps proportional to the negative of the gradient
A method to convert continuous target variables into binary labels
A technique to calculate dataset mean and variance
A sorting algorithm for multidimensional arrays
questions.explanation: Gradient Descent updates model weights in the direction opposite to the gradient of the loss function with respect to weights: $w \leftarrow w - \alpha \nabla L$.

questions.question: What is the difference between Precision and Recall?
options: Precision is the proportion of true positive predictions among all predicted positives; Recall is the proportion of true positives detected among all actual positives
Precision measures training speed; Recall measures testing accuracy
Recall is only used in regression problems
Precision is always higher than Recall
questions.explanation: Precision = TP / (TP + FP) (minimizes false alarms); Recall = TP / (TP + FN) (minimizes missed cases).

questions.question: What is the F1-Score?
options: The Harmonic Mean of Precision and Recall, providing a balanced metric especially on imbalanced datasets
The arithmetic average of True Positives and True Negatives
The percentage of correctly classified training samples
The ratio of learning rate to batch size
questions.explanation: F1 = 2 * (Precision * Recall) / (Precision + Recall), penalizing extreme imbalances between precision and recall.

questions.question: What is 'Data Leakage' in machine learning pipelines?
options: Information from outside the training dataset (such as target values or test distribution statistics) inadvertently used to train the model
A hacker stealing the dataset from server memory
Loss of training data rows due to corrupted disk sectors
Memory overflow during GPU tensor operations
questions.explanation: Data leakage occurs when features contain information that would not be available at inference time, creating artificially inflated evaluation metrics.

questions.question: What is K-Fold Cross-Validation?
options: Splitting data into K equal folds, training on K-1 folds and evaluating on the remaining fold, repeating K times to average performance
Training K different machine learning algorithms simultaneously
Scaling dataset features by a factor of K
Clustering data into K groups using K-Means
questions.explanation: K-fold CV ensures every data point is used for both training and validation, providing a robust estimate of generalization performance.

questions.question: What is the difference between One-Hot Encoding and Target (Mean) Encoding for high-cardinality categorical features?
options: One-Hot creates a binary column per category (causing curse of dimensionality); Target Encoding replaces categories with the mean target value for that category
Target encoding only works on text strings
One-hot encoding normalizes numbers to 0 and 1
Target encoding deletes missing values automatically
questions.explanation: One-hot encoding on 1,000 categories creates 1,000 sparse columns; target encoding replaces categories with their conditional target probability.

questions.question: What is the 'Curse of Dimensionality' in machine learning?
options: As the number of features increases, the feature space volume grows exponentially, causing data points to become sparse and distances equidistant
Datasets exceeding 1TB crashing standard laptops
Decision trees growing deeper than 100 levels
Neural networks consuming too much GPU electricity
questions.explanation: High dimensionality makes distance metrics (Euclidean) less discriminative and requires exponentially more samples to train models effectively.

questions.question: In Decision Trees, what is 'Gini Impurity' or 'Information Gain' (Entropy) used for?
options: Evaluating the quality of a split criterion to maximize class purity in child nodes
Measuring the depth of the tree in memory
Pruning leaf nodes based on CPU usage
Normalizing feature numerical scales
questions.explanation: Split algorithms (CART/C4.5) calculate Gini impurity or entropy reduction to select the feature and threshold that best separate classes.

questions.question: What is the difference between Batch Gradient Descent, Mini-Batch Gradient Descent, and Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD)?
options: Batch uses the entire dataset per update; SGD uses 1 sample per update; Mini-Batch uses a small batch (e.g. 32 or 64) balancing speed and stability
Batch only runs once; SGD runs forever
Mini-batch only works on small datasets under 1,000 rows
SGD is deterministic while Batch is random
questions.explanation: Mini-batch SGD combines vectorization speed of GPU hardware with smooth gradient convergence, making it the industry standard.

questions.question: What is the ROC curve (Receiver Operating Characteristic) and what does AUC measure?
options: Plots True Positive Rate against False Positive Rate across various probability classification thresholds; AUC measures overall ranking separability (1.0 is perfect)
Plots Training Loss against Validation Loss over epochs
Measures the correlation between independent variables
Plots residual errors in linear regression
questions.explanation: ROC-AUC evaluates binary classification discrimination threshold-independently; an AUC of 0.5 represents random guessing, while 1.0 represents perfect discrimination.
